title: Houthis Blockade Saudi Oil as US-Iran War Spreads to Red Sea
excerpt: Two tankers carrying Saudi crude to Asia reversed course after Yemen's Houthi rebels declared a naval blockade, threatening to trap most Gulf oil exports as war costs hit $37.5 billion.
body:
• Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, forcing two crude tankers bound for China and India to reverse course in the Red Sea
  • The blockade threatens the last major alternative route for Gulf oil after the Strait of Hormuz was effectively shut, pushing Brent crude above $91
  • Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told senators the war has cost $37.5 billion and asked Congress for $67 billion more in emergency funding
  • The US completed its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran; total American casualties stand at 18 killed and 447 wounded

A Second Chokepoint Under Threat

The US-Iran war opened a dangerous new front on Tuesday when two oil tankers loaded with Saudi crude made emergency U-turns in the Red Sea, the first tangible impact of a naval blockade declared by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels.

The tankers had just loaded Saudi crude at the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bound for China and India. After the Houthis sent letters to shippers threatening to attack any vessels loading or discharging Saudi oil, both reversed course toward the Suez Canal rather than sailing south through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

The blockade is a strategic escalation. Since the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shut by the war, Saudi Arabia had been piping millions of barrels per day to Yanbu on the Red Sea as an alternative export route. A full Houthi closure of that path could leave most Saudi oil exports trapped. Brent crude surged more than 2% on Tuesday, hovering above $91 a barrel, while US gasoline climbed back over $4 a gallon.

Eleven Nights of Strikes

US Central Command completed its 11th consecutive night of operations against Iran on Tuesday, targeting military operations centres, aircraft hangars, drone storage facilities and logistics infrastructure. Explosions were reported around Shiraz, Konarak, Chabahar and Qeshm Island. Strikes also expanded to northwestern Iran for the first time in the latest phase, hitting sites in Tabriz and Urmia.

"The developments represent the first confirmed changes to commercial tanker routing following the embargo and are likely to increase disruption to Saudi crude exports and regional shipping patterns."

— Vanguard, British maritime risk management group

US forces struck the Khojir Military Complex near Tehran for the first time — one of Iran's key research and manufacturing facilities for solid- and liquid-fuel missiles, according to ISW-CTP. Iran retaliated with strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan, and claimed to have targeted HIMARS systems at Camp Arifjan in Kuwait.

$37.5 Billion and Counting

In a heated Senate hearing, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth disclosed the war has cost an estimated $37.5 billion — up $9 billion since mid-May — and asked Congress to approve $67 billion in emergency supplemental funding. Democrats pushed back hard.

Sen. Patty Murray cited a Moody's Analytics estimate that the war has cost Americans at least $132 billion through rising prices, rate hikes and military spending. The Pentagon identified Sgt. Angel S. Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York, as killed in Iranian strikes at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. A second soldier, Sgt. Michael Emmanuel Swinton, 30, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, was killed during the detonation of a downed drone in Iraq. Total US casualties: 18 killed, 447 wounded.

Iran's War of Attrition

Tehran appears to be betting that time is on its side. Iranian authorities have maintained what they describe as a "proportional for now" response — retaliating against American interests or allied infrastructure for every strike on Iranian soil. Researcher Hamidreza Azizi of the Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik think tank characterised the conflict as "a contest against time and a war of endurance," noting the decisive question is whether Iran's deteriorating economy outpaces the pressure of rising global energy prices on Washington.

"Democrats pushed back hard.</p> <blockquote class="pull-quote"> <p>"You don't have a strategy."

For India, the dual-chokepoint crisis is particularly acute. One of the two tankers forced to turn back was carrying Saudi crude bound for India. With just four commodity vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Monday — down from a pre-war average of 130 — and the Red Sea route now threatened, India faces growing pressure on energy supplies.

Despite the escalation, diplomatic channels remain open. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran received a 10-day ceasefire proposal from mediators, and Iran's Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni visited Pakistan to continue mediation efforts. Trump warned the Houthis to back off. "If something like that happens, we take care of it," he said.
image_caption: Houthi forces have intensified their naval blockade in the Red Sea, disrupting global oil shipping routes and escalating the wider US-Iran conflict.
nri_angle: India faces growing energy supply pressure as one of the Saudi crude tankers forced to turn back in the Red Sea was bound for India, with both the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea routes now under threat.
author: Diaspora Desk
